answer: Because the timing is recorded against the harbor challenge, the jetty audit can replay the karst history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm hence has to pad 228 submissions and hold each account open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 22 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened.
